newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa recovering from heart op, wants to go home.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa recovering from heart op, wants to go home.

text.p: Mother Teresa, recovering from life-saving surgery to clear two coronary artery blockages, disagreed with doctors on her health on Saturday and said she was ready to go home, a senior medical official said.
"I am ready to go home. I am absolutely fine," A.K. Chatterjee, administrator of India's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre, quoted the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun as saying.
The latest medical bulletin issued by the clinic said Mother Teresa was "doing fairly well" but was not out of danger after Friday's surgery to fix the arterial blockages.
"She is conscious, alert, smiling and arguing with the medical staff. Her medical parameters are so far stabilising. She sat in a chair this morning," the bulletin added.
Chatterjee told reporters: "Perhaps in the next week we will be able to take a decision on her release".
Mother Teresa, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her devotion to the poor, underwent angiography and angioplasty for the third time since 1991.
Nuns at the Calcutta headquarters of Mother Teresa's Missionaries of Charity order said its members worldwide would hold special prayers for her on Saturday.
The Roman Catholic order, with about 4,500 nuns in more than 80 countries, was founded by Mother Teresa in 1949.
After Friday's surgery, an American doctor on Mother Teresa's team at the clinic said angioplasty had saved the life of the 1979 Nobel Peace prize winner.
Doctor Patricia Aubanel said some danger remained to her heart and it would take her up to three months to recover.
"She was going to have a heart attack -- a major heart attack -- if the angioplasty was not done," she told reporters.
"Mother could not have left the hospital alive without this angioplasty," said Aubanel, who treated her in California in 1991.
Angiography is an X-ray test which uses an injected opaque dye to show up blocked arteries. Angioplasty is the procedure to unblock the artery by inserting a balloon and inflating it.
The procedures were performed eight days after Mother Teresa, who was fitted with a pacemaker in 1989, entered hospital with an irregular heartbeat.
A medical bulletin issued after the angioplasty said the angiogram had shown "blockages in two major coronary arteries".
Mother Teresa previously had angiography and angioplasty in the United States in 1991 and at the Birla centre in 1993.
"She surprises everybody," Aubanel said on Friday. "She has amazing records of speedy recovery. At least on four earlier occasions she was nearly dead, but every time she recovered."
Doctors said Mother Teresa, born of Albanian parents as Gonxhe Bojaxhi, had suffered heart failure several times since entering the Woodlands Nursing Home in Calcutta on November 22.
She was moved to the Birla clinic last Tuesday.
